subject: Hyperscaler capital allocation and server CPU/platform cycles as distinct upstream demand axes for server DRAM and enterprise SSD

supported.finding: Microsoft's FY2024 Q4 source supports that the non-land/build portion of its cloud-and-AI spend was primarily servers, including CPUs and GPUs, deployed against customer demand signals.
supported.epistemic_boundary: Primary for Microsoft's own spend composition and procurement framing only; it does not quantify DRAM, NAND, HBM, enterprise-SSD bits, supplier share or supplier revenue.

supported.finding: Micron's June 2024 prepared remarks preserve a contemporaneous calendar-2024 server-unit growth expectation.
supported.epistemic_boundary: This is an Expectation/Judgment candidate, not realized server-shipment Reality and not a direct memory-bit forecast.

supported.finding: Micron reported annual new-product cadence on customer AI-server roadmaps.
supported.epistemic_boundary: Reported customer-roadmap cadence is not proof of actual shipment dates, installed-base replacement rate or memory consumption.

supported.finding: AMD's October 2024 5th Gen EPYC launch establishes a concrete server CPU platform generation with SP5 compatibility and a 12-channel DDR5 memory interface.
supported.epistemic_boundary: Technical platform facts do not establish adoption volume, populated DIMM count, DIMM capacity, DRAM bits per server, SSD attachment, enterprise-SSD capacity or total market demand.

supported.finding: The previously grounded Micron hyperscale-SSD source independently preserves Micron's contemporaneous assessment that hyperscale SSD demand was improving, driven primarily by AI training and inference infrastructure.
supported.epistemic_boundary: This is supplier management assessment of its market context; it does not prove that any named hyperscaler's capex flowed to Micron or provide an industry-wide NAND-bit coefficient.

not_established: No source in the grounded packet supplies a quantitative mapping from hyperscaler capex dollars to server DRAM bits, HBM bits, NAND bits, enterprise-SSD units or enterprise-SSD exabytes.
No source in the grounded packet supplies a quantitative mapping from a CPU/platform generation transition to DRAM content per server, SSD capacity per server or aggregate memory demand.
The server-unit growth statement is not realized shipment Reality and must not be combined with platform specifications to synthesize a memory-bit total.
Microsoft capex, Micron market assessment and AMD platform specifications are separate claim-scoped observations; cross-source temporal adjacency is not canonical causality.
No single 'data center demand' scalar is justified by this packet.
assessment.representation_decision: Represent hyperscaler capital allocation, server market expectations, server-product roadmap cadence, CPU/platform generation and memory/storage demand observations as separate typed claims with their own valid/known times. Create an explicit cross-industry relation only when a source states the bridge or when a future derived analytical layer is clearly labeled as a model rather than Reality.
assessment.canonical_projection_decision: Do not create new Reality predicates or a synthetic demand coefficient from this assessment. The current value is Evidence-level mechanism separation plus a curated research relation boundary.
assessment.outcome_for_ms0112: The lead is materially advanced: both upstream axes are independently grounded and semantically separable. The stronger claim that either axis quantitatively determines server DRAM or enterprise-SSD demand remains unresolved.

stop_rule.closed_search_surface: Do not repeat generic AI/data-center demand searches that merely restate capex growth, server growth or AI enthusiasm without supplying a claim-scoped bridge.
reopen_when: A hyperscaler or server OEM directly reports memory or storage content/procurement tied to a named server-platform vintage.
A methodological-primary server/memory source publishes memory-content-per-server or storage-content-per-server by platform generation with explicit methodology.
A supplier/customer primary source explicitly links a named platform transition to DRAM/HBM/NAND/enterprise-SSD procurement volume.

next_research_direction.principle: Prefer the next sealed Memory Atlas lead that adds a new mechanism or independent observation rather than elaborating MS-0112 with more correlated capex headlines.
next_research_direction.candidate_action: After closing seq110, recover the next high-importance unresolved cross-industry or counterfactual lead from the deterministic normalized lead index and admit it under existing semantic owners before new substantive work.
